servus, servī m.

noun, second declension

a slave

The ordinary word; a female slave is ancilla (serva is rare). Slavery is servitūs, servitūtis f.; to be a slave, servīre.

Other words

  • ancilla, ancillae f. — a female slave, a maid

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plaut., Ter.; Cic. Mil. 55 (Lewis & Short)

    The usual feminine of servus (Lewis & Short); in later and modern Latin a maidservant.

  • mancipium, mancipiī n. — a slave, as property

    noun, second declension · also used · classical

    A legal word: first the formal purchase by taking in hand, then the slave so bought; it treats the person as a thing owned.

Examples

  • ‘servī sunt.’ immō hominēs. ‘servī sunt.’ immō contubernālēs. ‘servī sunt.’ immō humilēs amīcī

    ‘They are slaves.’ No, they are people. ‘They are slaves.’ No, they share our roof. ‘They are slaves.’ No, they are humble friends.Sen. Ep. 47.1

  • Ulixēs domī etiam contumēliās servōrum ancillārumque pertulit

    at home Ulysses even put up with the insults of the slaves and the maidsCic. Off. 1.113 (Lewis & Short)

See also master.
